'''''Daphne odora''''', '''winter daphne''', is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] Thymelaeaceae, [[native plant|native]] to China, later spread to Japan and Korea. It is an [[evergreen]] shrub, grown for its very fragrant, fleshy, pale-pink, tubular flowers, each with four spreading lobes, and for its glossy [[foliage]]. It rarely fruits, producing red berries after flowering.

The Latin [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''odora'' means "fragrant".<ref name=RHSLG>{{cite book|last=Harrison|first=Lorraine|title=RHS Latin for gardeners|year=2012|publisher=Mitchell Beazley|location=United Kingdom|isbn=9781845337315|pages=224}}</ref> In Korea, the plant is also poetically called "chullihyang" – a thousand-mile scent – referring to the delightful fragrance of the flowers. In Japan, the plant is more commonly known as "[[wikt:沈丁花|jinchōge]]".

It grows best in fertile, slightly acid, peaty, well-drained soils. It grows in full sun or partial shade, and is hardy to {{convert|-10|C|F|abbr=on}}, possibly lower. 

Plants are not long lived, usually lasting eight to ten years.<ref>Flora, The Gardener's Bible, ABC Publishing, Sydney, 2005</ref> ''Daphne'' generally do not react well to root disturbance, and may transplant badly. ''D. odora'' is also susceptible to virus infection, which causes leaf mottling.<ref name = RD>The Reader's Digest Gardeners' Encyclopaedia of Plants & Flowers, Sydney, 1998</ref>

All parts of the plant are poisonous to humans and to a range of domestic animals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.anbg.gov.au/poison-plants/D-poison.html|title = Poison Plant Illustrations - Australian Plant Information}}</ref> Some people experience dermatitis from contact with the sap.<ref>[https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/56422/Daphne-odora-Aureomarginata-(v)/Details Royal Horticultural Society ] </ref>

''Daphne odora'' may be propagated by semi-ripe cuttings in summer.

==Cultivars==
*''D. odora'' [[form (botany)|f.]] ''rosacea'' has white and pink flowers.
*''D. odora'' f. ''rubra'' has dark red-pink flowers with reduced fragrance.
*''D. odora'' 'Aureomarginata' has yellow edged leaves, and is hardier and more suitable to cultivation than the plain-leaved forms.<ref name = RD />
